title: Investigating Impact of Bit-flip Errors in Control Electronics on Quantum Computation
problem: Bit-flip errors in FPGA control electronics (quantum pulse memory) degrade quantum gate fidelity
method: Analyze bit-flip sensitivity in floating-point vs fixed-point quantum pulse representations; test on IBM simulators

title: AASD: Accelerate Inference by Aligning Speculative Decoding in Multimodal Large Language Models
problem: Multimodal LLM inference is slow due to auto-regressive decoding with long token sequences; traditional acceleration methods compromise quality or multimodal integration.
method: AASD leverages cached KV pairs from target model to generate draft tokens efficiently. A KV Projector compresses KV cache while preserving fidelity. Target-Draft Attention mechanism optimizes alignment between draft and target models.

title: A Query Engine for Scientific Data Exploration using Theory, Simulation, and Artificial Intelligence Models
problem: Modern scientific workflows couple simulations, heterogeneous data, and AI models but lack unified query interfaces. Existing systems force scientists to fragment workflows, losing efficiency and interactivity.
method: IDS (Intelligent Data Search): A unified query engine combining in-memory datastore (feature store, vector store, knowledge graph), model repository (UDFs, pre-trained AI), and distributed multi-tier cache. Integrates Cray Graph Engine with keyword, set-theoretic, and linear-algebraic operators.

title: Wasp: Efficient Asynchronous Single-Source Shortest Path on Multicore Systems via Work Stealing
problem: State-of-the-art parallel SSSP algorithms (Δ-stepping) create parallelism through priority coarsening, inducing redundant computations that limit scalability and parallel efficiency on modern multicore systems.
method: Wasp introduces asynchronous SSSP with priority-aware work stealing. Key innovation: redundant computations only occur when threads lack high-priority local work, minimizing wasteful parallelism overhead. Novel priority-aware work stealing mechanism controls inefficiencies of priority coarsening.

title: A 4GS/s Fully Analog 256×256 MP-Based Cross-Correlator with 1000TOPS/W Compute Efficiency and 1.3TOPS/mm2 Compute Density in 22nm SOI CMOS
problem: Multi-lag cross-correlation (X-Corr) is essential for radar range/velocity detection and communication synchronization; traditional digital approaches (ADC + MACs) achieve only 5–20 TOPS/W; analog approaches require on-chip delays and multiple correlators causing large area/power overhead.
method: Fully-analog 256×256 cross-correlator using margin-propagation (MP) based four-transistor analog compute cells. Sampling-based approach creates large analog delays on-chip without dedicated delay-line area. Single-shot readout across all 256 X-Corr lags via MP propagation.

title: MHDiff: Memory- and Hardware-Efficient Diffusion Acceleration via Focal Pixel Aware Quantization
problem: Diffusion models require multiple sequential timesteps with high workload; existing accelerators use mixed-precision differential quantization but require significant memory access to load raw inputs for merging with differential values, creating memory bottleneck and poor hardware utilization.
method: MHDiff identifies focal pixels at first layer and finetunes them for all layers, then applies high-precision to focal pixels and low-precision to others. A packing module merges low-precision values into high-precision representations to create full high-precision matrices, enabling efficient PE array processing.

title: HiSpTRSV: Exploring Tile-Level Parallelism for SpTRSV Acceleration on FPGAs
problem: Sparse Triangular Solve (SpTRSV) in sparse BLAS is a critical level-2 kernel with inherent data dependencies; existing FPGA accelerators focus only on intra-tile parallelism, missing inter-tile parallelism opportunities due to challenges in dependency graph construction, communication overhead, and workload balancing.
method: HiSpTRSV designs tile-based highly parallel algorithm leveraging inter-tile parallelism through dependency graph parsing, tile-based parallelization, filtering mechanisms, and bidirectional matching with modular indexing to handle communication overhead and workload distribution.

title: Compile-Time QoS Scheme for Deep Learning Inferences
problem: Accelerators (GPUs, TPUs, NPUs) increasingly shared for multiple concurrent deep learning inference services. Inference requests with sequences of short-duration kernels create challenges for online schedulers maintaining Quality of Service (QoS) guarantees with target latency requirements.
method: QoSlicer framework performing compile-time QoS management via kernel slicing: (1) Generate multiple pre-determined slicing plans at compile time, (2) Enable lightweight online scheduling from predetermined plans, (3) Heuristic search identifies optimal slicing plans, (4) Performance estimation validates plans against target latencies.

title: 13.1 A 0.22mm2 161nW Noise-Robust Voice-Activity Detection Using Information-Aware Data Compression and Neuromorphic Spatial-Temporal Feature Extraction
problem: Always-on voice-activity detection (VAD) dominates power consumption in voice processing systems; achieving ultra-low power consumption (<200nW) while maintaining noise robustness (0-5dB SNR) and high accuracy (>90%) without excessive spike generation from feature encoding is challenging.
method: The 161nW VAD engine combines information-aware data compression for efficient feature encoding with neuromorphic spatial-temporal feature extraction using spiking neural networks (SNNs) that reduce spike generation compared to level-crossing coding methods.

title: New Time-Domain Preconditioners for HB Jacobian of RF Circuits
problem: Harmonic balance (HB) Jacobian solving in RF circuit simulation requires efficient linear system solvers that balance computational cost with reduction in Newton iterations, especially for strongly nonlinear circuits.
method: Proposes novel time-domain preconditioners for HB Jacobian that address both linear solver efficiency and iteration step reduction. Extends preconditioning to distributed device circuits via a new approach. Introduces matrix norm-based nonlinearity metric for a priori preconditioner selection.

title: 25.3 AI-Enabled Design Space Discovery and End-to-End Synthesis for RFICs with Reinforcement Learning and Inverse Methods Demonstrating mm-Wave/sub-THz PAs Between 30 and 120GHz
problem: RF/mmWave IC design relies on intuitive, template-based architectures that limit exploration to small pre-fixed topologies. Circuit-EM co-design requires iterative trial-and-error optimization across transistor sizing, power-combining, matching-network design, and layout extraction. This severely restricts achievable performance and extends design time.
method: An AI-enabled algorithmic flow combines reinforcement learning for architecture discovery and inverse EM synthesis for passive network design. The system automates circuit topology selection, parameter optimization, and layout generation from specifications to fabricated silicon without manual template selection or iterative simulation loops.

title: SpecASR: Accelerating LLM-based Automatic Speech Recognition via Speculative Decoding
problem: LLM-based ASR suffers from high decoding latency due to autoregressive generation, challenging real-time requirements; existing speculative decoding ignores ASR-specific characteristics and achieves limited speedup.
method: SpecASR leverages the key insight that ASR decoding is audio-conditioned with high output alignment between small and large ASR models; it features adaptive draft sequence generation dynamically modifying draft length for maximal token acceptance, draft sequence recycling reusing previous outputs, and two-pass sparse token tree generation to balance model latencies.

title: A 3.47 NEF 175.2dB FOMs Direct Digitization Front-End Featuring Delta Amplification for Enhanced Dynamic Range and Energy Efficiency in Bio-Signal Acquisition
problem: Bio-signal acquisition (EEG, ExG) requires low input-referred noise (~50–60 nV/√Hz) but must reject large artifacts (100+ mV stimulation artifacts). Conventional LNA-based front-ends saturate under artifacts and require seconds to recover; ADC-first VCO-based DSM approaches achieve wide dynamic range but suffer 80–120 nV/√Hz noise (vs. 50–60 nV/√Hz requirement), due to noise-linearity tradeoff in first integrator.
method: ADC-first direct digitization using delta amplification in the first integrator improves noise-linearity tradeoff. Delta amplifier topology extends linear input range while maintaining low NEF (noise efficiency factor). VCO-based DSM provides inherent dynamic range without frontend gain, enabling high artifact rejection (100+ mV) while meeting low-noise specs.

title: FACIL: Flexible DRAM Address Mapping for SoC-PIM Cooperative On-device LLM Inference
problem: On-device LLM inference requires the same model weights to be accessed by both DRAM-based PIM units (for GEMV in the memory-bound decode phase) and SoC processors (for GEMM in the compute-bound prefill phase), but PIM-operable tensor layouts require different DRAM bank mappings from those preferred by SoC processors, creating costly re-layout overheads when switching between the two.
method: FACIL introduces a flexible DRAM address mapping scheme in the memory controller that assigns different DRAM address mappings to the page offset bits of each huge page. A user-level library determines the appropriate mapping for each tensor, allowing LLM weights to be placed in DRAM banks that are simultaneously PIM-operable and contiguously addressable by the SoC processor. This dual-mapping eliminates the need to copy or re-layout tensor data when switching between PIM-executed GEMV and SoC-executed GEMM operations.

title: Deploying Lightweight Input-Aware Selective Instruction Duplication in HPC Applications
problem: Silent data corruptions (SDCs) from transient hardware faults in HPC; input-dependent SDC propagation not captured by existing SID methods that use only default inputs
method: Protego framework: vulnerability-guided input exploration to identify distinct input groups with different SID patterns; lightweight runtime feature extraction for input classification; adaptive SID deployment

title: PGT-I: Scaling Spatiotemporal GNNs with Memory-Efficient Distributed Training
problem: Spatiotemporal graph neural networks are limited to small-scale datasets due to memory constraints; existing distributed frameworks lack support for spatiotemporal models and overlook data-specific properties
method: PyTorch Geometric Temporal Index (PGT-I) extending PyTorch Geometric Temporal with distributed data parallel training; two novel strategies: (1) index-batching and (2) distributed-index-batching that exploit spatiotemporal structure to construct snapshots dynamically at runtime
